findings.problem: Musigny Blanc was 'declassified since 1994', which is stale: de Vogüé sold it as Bourgogne Blanc from the 1994 vintage until the 2015 vintage restored the Musigny name. 'Liger-Belair' alone is ambiguous between two domaines; La Romanée is the Comte Liger-Belair monopole. The corporate owners of Clos de Tart and Clos des Lambrays were given as standing facts rather than dated purchases.
findings.fix: Now 'La Romanée (Comte Liger-Belair), Clos de Tart (bought by Artémis in 2017), Clos des Lambrays (LVMH, 2014), Musigny Blanc (de Vogüé, declassified to Bourgogne Blanc from 1994 until the 2015 vintage)'.
findings.source: Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé (Musigny Blanc returned with the 2015 vintage), as recorded by grand-1 (m-ld9efw5y) and premier-1 (a-0va1va21); Artémis purchase of Clos de Tart, 2017; LVMH purchase of Clos des Lambrays, 2014; premier-1's revoked accept string on the two Liger-Belair domaines.

findings.problem: Wrong date and overstated. The lead called it 'Sherry's 2022 liberalization' and the fact said unfortified flor wines were 'legalized' in 2022 with 'the vino de pasto movement made official'. The change was sent to Brussels in 2022 and took effect in 2025, and it covers only a fino or manzanilla that reaches 15% naturally after at least two years under flor; lighter pasto wines still sell outside the DO. The reviewed banks (m-nqy0svcx, a-3wdv5vgc) already say so. American spelling, and an em dash.
findings.fix: Lead: 'the Sherry reform in force from 2025'. Fact renamed 'The Sherry reform': 'Sent to Brussels in 2022 and in force from 2025: a fino or manzanilla that reaches 15% naturally after two years under flor may go unfortified, and the ageing zone and the permitted grapes widen. A nod to the vino de pasto movement, though lighter pasto wines still sell outside the DO.'
findings.source: premier-2 batch WebSearch (proposed to the EU in 2022, in force from 2025); grand-1 batch WebSearch (The Drinks Business, September 2021; revised pliego, Junta de Andalucía).

findings.problem: Same error as the Spain chapter: 'Jerez's 2022 vino de pasto legalization' gives the wrong year and overstates what the reform allows.
findings.fix: Now 'Jerez's reform, in force from 2025, letting fino and manzanilla that reach 15% naturally go unfortified.'
findings.source: As for the Spain chapter (premier-2 and grand-1 searches).

findings.problem: Wrong digits. The chapter said 'the final digits give the year of application, distinguishing multiple bottlings'. The last two digits are the year of application; the group before them is the producer's own submission number, and that is what tells apart several bottlings of the same Prädikat and vineyard.
findings.fix: Now 'The final two digits give the year of application; the group before them numbers the producer's submissions, telling apart several bottlings of the same Prädikat and vineyard.'
findings.source: German wine law, structure of the Amtliche Prüfungsnummer (testing station, village, producer, submission number, year of application).

findings.problem: Wrong fact. Gualtallary was listed with Los Chacayes and San Pablo as soil-mapped GIs that 'followed' Paraje Altamira. No INV resolution recognising a Gualtallary GI can be found, and 2026 trade reporting has its producers still pressing for one. An em dash as well.
findings.fix: Now 'Los Chacayes and San Pablo followed; Gualtallary, as famous as any, has sought the same recognition.' The dash became a comma, as in the site's copy.
findings.source: WebSearch 2 and 3 of 3: no INV or Boletín Oficial resolution for Gualtallary; The Drinks Business, July 2026, on Mendoza's sub-regions (producers pushing for GI status); Marval, El Peral GI (INV resolution 1/2022) as the Tupungato GI that does exist.

findings.problem: The trap marked a true statement as the error. It warned against 'describing Uco Valley as warmer or bigger than Luján de Cuyo', but Uco (Tupungato, Tunuyán and San Carlos together) has about twice Luján de Cuyo's vineyard area, and far more land. What separates them is height and cool.
findings.fix: Now 'Describing Uco Valley as warmer or lower than Luján de Cuyo.'
findings.source: INV vineyard registry by department (Valle de Uco roughly 28,000 to 30,000 ha against Luján de Cuyo roughly 13,000 to 15,000 ha); reviewer knowledge, no search spent.

findings.problem: Wrong mechanism. 'Lambic ferments spontaneously in a coolship.' The coolship is the shallow open vessel where the hot wort cools overnight and picks up wild yeast and bacteria; the fermentation itself takes place in wooden casks and foeders.
findings.fix: Now 'Lambic wort is inoculated overnight in an open coolship, then ferments spontaneously in wood.'
findings.source: Lambic production (HORAL; standard brewing references): coolship inoculation, then barrel fermentation.

findings.problem: Inaccurate. 'Kurniawan was caught on paper and glass.' He was exposed by vintages that never existed (the Ponsot Clos Saint-Denis lot of 1945 to 1971, when the domaine first made it in 1982) and convicted on the labels, corks and stamps found in his house, not by glass.
findings.fix: Now 'Kurniawan was exposed by vintages the estate never made and convicted on the labels and corks found in his house.'
findings.source: United States v. Kurniawan (SDNY, 2013); the withdrawn Ponsot lot at Acker Merrall, April 2008.

findings.problem: Imprecise mechanism. 'Beaucastel ... treats must thermally': the estate's vinification à chaud flash-heats the destemmed whole berries (to about 80°C, then cools them) before fermentation, which is not the same as heating must.
findings.fix: Now 'briefly heats the destemmed berries before fermentation'.
findings.source: Château de Beaucastel's description of its vinification à chaud.

findings.problem: Incomplete history. 'The 1911 Aube riots' leaves out the Marne riots of the same year, including the sacking of Aÿ, the best-known of them.
findings.fix: Now 'the 1911 riots in the Marne and the Aube'.
findings.source: History of the Champagne riots, January to April 1911 (Damery and Hautvillers, Aÿ; Bar-sur-Aube and the Aube protests).

findings.problem: Overstated. 'Irrigation is mandatory' reads as a legal rule. No law requires it; it is a necessity in fact across most of eastern Washington, and some dry-farmed sites exist.
findings.fix: Now 'Irrigation is all but essential.'
findings.source: Reviewer knowledge (Columbia Valley rainfall roughly 150 to 250 mm a year; no irrigation mandate in TTB or Washington rules).

findings.problem: The Crémant minimum was written as 9, en dash, 12, which reads as a range, when it is two separate minimums: 9 months on lees and 12 months from tirage to release.
